title: Coral and the Promise
premise: Rafael Blackwood, a wedding planner who abandoned his own engagement eleven years ago, receives a letter lost in the mail since then — written by Coral, the woman he left, and postmarked the week he vanished. He tracks her to a fading seaside town where she runs a bakery on the edge of losing its lease, and he arrives posing as a client planning a wedding that isn't real. As the false wedding becomes the town's hope and Coral's last chance to save the bakery, Rafael must choose between protecting her with silence and confessing that the letter — and the man who wrote back too late — is him. In the end, he tells the truth on what was meant to be the fake wedding day; Coral nearly turns him away, but chooses the man he has become over the boy who fled, and they sign the bakery lease together as the last train leaves without either of them.
about_author: Felix Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former hospitality manager who spent a decade orchestrating other people's perfect days before turning to fiction. He writes love stories about second chances from a small coastal apartment, where he insists the sea air improves his prose.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. A water-stained letter arrives at Rafael's London office, addressed to him but written by Coral Hartley eleven years ago — the week he ended their engagement by disappearing. Reading it reopens everything he buried. Emotional beat: dread and longing colliding; the safe life he built begins to crack at its foundation.

chapters.title: The Town That Smells of Bread
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael follows the return address to Saltmere Bay, telling himself he'll only look. He finds Coral's bakery thriving on nostalgia but failing on numbers, and Coral herself guarded, brilliant, and unrecognizable in all the ways that matter. Emotional beat: bittersweet awe; he watches her through glass, unable to walk in.

chapters.title: A Wedding Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A stranger walks into the bakery claiming to plan a society wedding and wants it hosted in Saltmere Bay — with her ovens catering. Coral smells something off about Rafael Blackwood but needs the commission before the lease expires in eight weeks. Emotional beat: wary hope; she takes the deal she doesn't trust.

chapters.title: Measurements and Old Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Planning meetings force proximity: tasting cakes, measuring the village hall, arguing over peonies. Rafael keeps almost confessing; Coral notices he flinches at her name. A near-kiss over a ruined sponge cake. Emotional beat: magnetic tension; two people circling a fire both remember being burned by.

chapters.title: The Lease Clause
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral discovers the landlord plans to sell to a developer regardless of revenue — unless the wedding brings the town together enough to fight. Meanwhile she finds an old photograph of Rafael with a woman wearing a ring she recognizes as one she once lost. Emotional beat: rising suspicion braided with desperation.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Flashback chapter: the full text of Coral's eleven-year-old letter — she had been pregnant, had lost the baby alone, and begged him to come home. Rafael reveals to his business partner why he never got it: he'd changed addresses out of shame. Emotional beat: devastating guilt; the reader now knows what Coral doesn't.

chapters.title: Storm Over Saltmere
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A storm floods the bakery days before the wedding; the whole town turns out to save it, and Rafael works beside Coral until dawn, soaked and honest-seeming. She lets him stay after the last train leaves — couch, blanket, walls down. Emotional beat: tenderness breaking through; almost-love, almost-truth.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner Lie
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. At the rehearsal dinner, Coral's brother recognizes Rafael from the old engagement photo and confronts him privately: tell her, or I will. Rafael stalls, and Coral overhears enough to shatter — the wedding is fake, the planner is her ghost. Emotional beat: betrayal detonating; everything built collapses in one room.

chapters.title: The Empty Aisle
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Wedding day arrives with no bride, no groom, and a town expecting a miracle. Coral decides to hold the event anyway for the lease fight — until Rafael stands up in front of everyone and tells the whole truth: the letter, the baby, the cowardice, the years. Emotional beat: climax; raw public confession, her choice suspended.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Coral walks out; Rafael waits three days at the bakery door like a man keeping a promise instead of breaking one. She returns not with forgiveness finished but with a decision begun — they sign the new lease together, co-owners, and let the last train leave empty. Emotional beat: earned resolution; belonging chosen, not inherited.
